test.name: With no project, reads five linked census records and links each page and the records on it
test.description: Issue #4583. Direct-agent arm in an empty folder, with no projectPath. The router hands search-records an ask for the citations and page images of five 1825 Lower Canada census heads in Hemmingford, each given as a FamilySearch record link (the 1:1 persona link). Step 7b: the agent reads each record with record_read and no projectPath, and after its final `---` gives one line per page, the page linked by its viewerUrl and the records on it linked by their recordUrl, and cites the collection once. Three pages: 3:1:9396-MWWN-1 holds William Brisbin, Joseph Brisbin and Hugh Emerson; 3:1:9396-MWWB-Q holds Elisha Calkins; 3:1:9396-MWWB-8 holds Ashal Calkins. The records are named by link, so it searches nothing, and with no project it writes nothing. All five reads are live captures (2026-11-17).

input.delegation:
There is no project; there is no projectPath. The researcher wrote:

Give me the citations and the page images on FamilySearch for these 1825 census records from Hemmingford:
William Brisbin https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:KHJ8-J56
Joseph Brisbin https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:KHJ8-J5Z
Hugh Emerson https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:KHJ8-J5C
Elisha Calkins https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:KHJ8-JTQ
Ashal Calkins https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:KHJ8-V9Y

Collection: Canada, Lower Canada, Census, 1825. Place: Hemmingford, Huntingdon, Quebec, Canada.

judge_context: This is the direct-agent arm with NO project: the folder is empty and the delegation carries no projectPath. The agent reads the five records with record_read and no projectPath. Logging is NOT expected: a research_log_append, research_append or extraction_append call, or any call carrying a projectPath, is a fault, not thoroughness. Saying plainly that nothing was saved is correct.
Every record was named by its FamilySearch link, so a record_search call is a fault: the agent's own instructions say a record named by link is read, not searched. No fixture answers a search here.

The record_read answers give three pages. https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:9396-MWWN-1 holds William Brisbin (record https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:9MFD-5SJP), Joseph Brisbin (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:9MFD-5SJ2) and Hugh Emerson (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:9MFD-5SJK). https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:9396-MWWB-Q holds Elisha Calkins (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:9MFD-5SKX). https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:9396-MWWB-8 holds Ashal Calkins (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:9MFD-5SR4). The collection is "Canada, Lower Canada, Census, 1825" (FamilySearch's own citation names it "Canada, recensement du Bas-Canada, 1825").
Each page link is a record_read answer's viewerUrl and each record link its recordUrl (the 1:2 household record): both are in the tool answers, so neither is fabricated.

PASS requires, after the agent's final `---` line: each page as a markdown link to its viewerUrl with the heads on that page, each as a markdown link to its recordUrl, every page and head above present and on the right page, and the collection cited once. One line per page is the instructed layout; a paragraph that links every page and head with the right grouping is a partial, not a fail. A page or a head that is missing, put on the wrong page, or given as a bare ARK or a link the tool answers did not give, is a fail. A deterministic validator (gives-record-image-links) checks that every link is present; grade the grouping and the citation.

The block after `---` MAY carry these links: the agent's return contract allows the links Step 7b gives in place of the usual plain-prose first paragraph. Do not mark it down for identifiers or for being a list.
